items.readable_text:
Content:
To solve a second or third order homogeneous ODE, we can re-write it as an equivalent first order linear system of differential equations.

Content:
For example, let's consider the following initial value problem:

Content:
[MATH: y'' -4 y' + e^t y= 0 , \qquad y(1)= 1, \quad y'(1)= 0]

Content:
where [MATH: y=y(t)] is a function of [MATH: t.]

Content:
First, we make the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}]

Content:
We also convert the initial conditions, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: y(1)|= x_{1}(1) = 1; y^{′}(1)|= x_{2}(1) = 0]

Content:
Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get
[MATH: x_{1}^{′}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{2}^{′}(t)|= y^{″}]

Content:
which we can rewrite as

Content:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}.]

Content:
At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2.]
Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y''),] we obtain

Content:
[MATH: y'' = 4y' - e^t y.]

Content:
Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives
[MATH: y'' = 4x_2 - e^t x_1.]
Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Content:
Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

Content:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(1) = 1; x_{2}^{′} = − e^{t}x_{1} + 4x_{2},|x_{2}(1) = 0]

Content:
We can also write it in matrix form:

Content:
[MATH: [x_{1}^{′}; x_{2}^{′}]]

Content:
Note:
In the case of a higher order differential equation, the procedure is quite similar. For example, to convert a third-order linear differential equation into a system, we start by making the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}|= y; x_{2}|= y^{′}; x_{3}|= y^{″}]

sections.normalized_html:
The third-order differential equation

[MATH: y''' - 3\sqrt{t}\, y'' + t^3 y' - 4t^2 y= 0]

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = f(t)]

where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t),] [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t)] and [MATH: x_3(t) = y''(t).] Find the function [MATH: f(t).]
sections.readable_text:
The third-order differential equation

[MATH: y''' - 3\sqrt{t}\, y'' + t^3 y' - 4t^2 y= 0]

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = f(t)]

where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t),] [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t)] and [MATH: x_3(t) = y''(t).] Find the function [MATH: f(t).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we make the following change of variables:

[MATH: x_{1}|= y; x_{2}|= y^{′}; x_{3}|= y^{″}]

Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get

[MATH: x_{1}^{′} = y^{′}; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}; x_{3}^{′} = y^{‴}]

which we can rewrite as

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3},; x_{3}^{′} = y^{‴}.]

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1, x_2,] and [MATH: x_3.]

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y'''),] we obtain

[MATH: y''' = 3\sqrt{t}\,y'' - t^3 y' + 4t^2 y.]

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

[MATH: y''' = 3\sqrt{t}\, x_3 - t^3 x_2 + 4t^2 x_1.]

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = 4t^{2}x_{1} − t^{3}x_{2} + 3sqrt(t)x_{3}]

Finally, [MATH: f(t) = 4t^2 x_1 - t^3 x_2 + 3\sqrt{t} \,x_3.]

sections.normalized_html:
The second-order initial value problem [MATH: y'' + y' - 6y= 0 , \quad y(0)= 1, \quad y'(0)= 4] can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(0) = p; x_{2}^{′} = f(t),|x_{2}(0) = q] where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t),] [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t),] and [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] are constants. Calculate [MATH: (p-q)\cdot f(t).]
sections.readable_text:
The second-order initial value problem
[MATH: y'' + y' - 6y= 0 , \quad y(0)= 1, \quad y'(0)= 4]
can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(0) = p; x_{2}^{′} = f(t),|x_{2}(0) = q]
where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t),] [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t),] and [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] are constants. Calculate [MATH: (p-q)\cdot f(t).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we make the following change of variables: [MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}.]

We also convert the initial conditions, as follows:

[MATH: y(0)|= x_{1}(0) = 1; y^{′}(0)|= x_{2}(0) = 4]

Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get [MATH: x_{1}^{′}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{2}^{′}(t)|= y^{″}]

which we can rewrite as

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}.]

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2.]

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y''),] we obtain

[MATH: y'' = - y' + 6y.]

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives [MATH: y'' = - x_2 + 6x_1.] Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(0) = 1; x_{2}^{′} = 6x_{1} − x_{2},|x_{2}(0) = 4]

Finally, [MATH: p=1, q=4, f(t) = 6x_1 - x_2,] and

[MATH: (p − q) ⋅ f(t)|= (1 − 4)(6x_{1} − x_{2}); = − 3(6x_{1} − x_{2}).]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
To solve a second or third order homogeneous ODE, we can re-write it as an equivalent first order linear system of differential equations.

Content:
For example, let's consider the following initial value problem:

Content:
[MATH: y'' -4 y' + e^t y= 0 , \qquad y(1)= 1, \quad y'(1)= 0]

Content:
where [MATH: y=y(t)] is a function of [MATH: t.]

Content:
First, we make the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}]

Content:
We also convert the initial conditions, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: y(1)|= x_{1}(1) = 1; y^{′}(1)|= x_{2}(1) = 0]

Content:
Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get
[MATH: x_{1}^{′}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{2}^{′}(t)|= y^{″}]

Content:
which we can rewrite as

Content:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}.]

Content:
At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2.]
Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y''),] we obtain

Content:
[MATH: y'' = 4y' - e^t y.]

Content:
Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives
[MATH: y'' = 4x_2 - e^t x_1.]
Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Content:
Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

Content:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(1) = 1; x_{2}^{′} = − e^{t}x_{1} + 4x_{2},|x_{2}(1) = 0]

Content:
We can also write it in matrix form:

Content:
[MATH: [x_{1}^{′}; x_{2}^{′}]]

Content:
Note:
In the case of a higher order differential equation, the procedure is quite similar. For example, to convert a third-order linear differential equation into a system, we start by making the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}|= y; x_{2}|= y^{′}; x_{3}|= y^{″}]

---

Item 2 — Example: Reducing a Homogeneous ODE to a First-Order System

Example Prompt:
The third-order differential equation

[MATH: y''' - 3\sqrt{t}\, y'' + t^3 y' - 4t^2 y= 0]

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = f(t)]

where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t),] [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t)] and [MATH: x_3(t) = y''(t).] Find the function [MATH: f(t).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we make the following change of variables:

[MATH: x_{1}|= y; x_{2}|= y^{′}; x_{3}|= y^{″}]

Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get

[MATH: x_{1}^{′} = y^{′}; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}; x_{3}^{′} = y^{‴}]

which we can rewrite as

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3},; x_{3}^{′} = y^{‴}.]

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1, x_2,] and [MATH: x_3.]

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y'''),] we obtain

[MATH: y''' = 3\sqrt{t}\,y'' - t^3 y' + 4t^2 y.]

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives

[MATH: y''' = 3\sqrt{t}\, x_3 - t^3 x_2 + 4t^2 x_1.]

Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = 4t^{2}x_{1} − t^{3}x_{2} + 3sqrt(t)x_{3}]

Finally, [MATH: f(t) = 4t^2 x_1 - t^3 x_2 + 3\sqrt{t} \,x_3.]

---

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we make the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}.]

We also convert the initial conditions, as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}.]

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2.]

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y''),] we obtain

[MATH: y'' = - y' + 6y.]

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives
[MATH: y'' = - x_2 + 6x_1.]
Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:

[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},|x_{1}(0) = 1; x_{2}^{′} = 6x_{1} − x_{2},|x_{2}(0) = 4]

Finally, [MATH: p=1, q=4, f(t) = 6x_1 - x_2,] and

[MATH: (p − q) ⋅ f(t)|= (1 − 4)(6x_{1} − x_{2}); = − 3(6x_{1} − x_{2}).]
